successors.name: Konbaung dynasty
successors.text: Arakan, taken when the Burmese 'captured the Arakanese capital, Mrauk-U, on January 2, 1785'

ledger.x: April 1429: Min Saw Mon is proclaimed king at Launggyet, founding the Arakanese kingdom of Mrauk U.
13 April 1533: Min Bin leaves Dhaka for Mrauk-U.
28 October 1546: Toungoo invades Arakan by land and sea with about 19,000 men, taking Thandwe; Mrauk-U is surrounded on 24 January 1547 and the siege fails.
9 September 1580: a Toungoo force of 24,000 under Bayinnaung's son Thiri Thudhamma Yaza 'quickly seized Thandwe'; it laid siege to Mrauk-U for over a year without breaking the fort.
November 1581: the invasion is called off after Bayinnaung's death in November 1581.
December 1599: Pegu surrenders to the Arakanese.
About March 1600: the Arakanese leave Pegu.
March 1603: De Brito revolts at Syriam and the Lower Burmese coast is lost.
2 January 1785: the Kingdom of Mrauk U ends.

wars.name: Bengal-Arakan war of 1459
wars.outcome: 'A war with Arakan in 1459 led to the defeat of Bengali Sultan Rukunuddin Barbak Shah'; Arakan holds Chittagong until 1516 (infobox: conquest of Chittagong 1459).

wars.name: Bengal-Arakan war of 1512-1516
wars.outcome: Hussain Shah 'restored Bengali sovereignty in Chittagong and northern Arakan'; Chittagong leaves the Arakanese outline in 1516.

wars.name: Arakanese invasion of Bengal
wars.outcome: Min Bin takes Chittagong (October 1532) and enters Dhaka (11 December 1532), leaving on 13 April 1533; his control beyond Chittagong was 'largely nominal'.

wars.name: Toungoo invasion of Arakan (1545-1547)
wars.outcome: Toungoo took Thandwe and besieged Mrauk-U (24-30 January 1547) but was flooded out; truce 30 January, retreat 2 February, Thandwe evacuated 26 March 1547.

wars.name: Arakanese-Tripuran wars
wars.outcome: Tripura 'agreed to pay tribute' after its capital fell in January 1575; it joined the Chittagong rebellion of 1586 and submitted again 'within two weeks'; by February 1596 Razagyi had 'reestablished control over Tripura'.

wars.name: Toungoo invasion of Arakan (1580-1581)
wars.outcome: Toungoo seized Thandwe on 9 September 1580 and besieged Mrauk-U for over a year; the invasion was 'called off after Bayinnaung died in November 1581'.

wars.name: Arakanese conquest of Lower Burma
wars.outcome: Syriam seized in March 1599, Pegu surrendered in December 1599 and was burned about March 1600; De Brito revolted at Syriam in March 1603 and the Lower Burmese coast was lost.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Chittagong
wars.outcome: Sandwip fell in November 1665 and Anderkilla on 27 January 1666; Chittagong became a Mughal faujdar's seat.

wars.name: Konbaung conquest of Arakan
wars.outcome: Thado Minsaw's army of over 20,000 took Mrauk-U on 2 January 1785 and ended the kingdom; about 35,000 Rakhine fled to British Bengal.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty frontier appears on any page opened; the Naf/Kaladan line after 1666 is given two ways.
